chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the carcass (ramiyyah) that its owner finds the next day: is it permissible to eat? He said, 'If he knows that his shot was what killed it, then let him eat, and that is if he had recited the name [of God].'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الرَّمِيَّةِ: Carcass or dead animal, specifically one that died without ritual slaughter
key_terms.سَمَّى: He recited the name of God (Tasmiyah)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat an animal found dead the next day after hunting?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the condition of 'certainty' (yaqeen) in hunting, distinguishing it from mere probability, which is crucial in Shia fiqh for determining the permissibility of game found later. It reinforces the necessity of the initial invocation (tasmiyah) at the moment of the shot, linking the physical act of hunting to its spiritual validity. This ruling is foundational in the chapter of hunting (al-Sayd) within al-Tusi's Tahdhib, emphasizing the hunter's responsibility in verifying the cause of death.
